overview: After 1.d4 d5 White plays 2.g4, offering a pawn for a kingside space grab. Black can take with ...Bxg4 and enjoys a healthy extra pawn, while White hopes for quick development and attacking chances against an exposed Black king.

white_ideas.idea: Bishop on g2 and rapid development
Harry the king with h4 and g5
Win back the pawn with Nf3 and Qd3

typical_structures.structure: Open centre; White kingside pawns advanced early

character.notes: Wild attacking attempts, but the extra pawn gives Black an easy game.

gambit.notes: g4 can be taken by ...Bxg4 and White gets modest compensation.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider it unsound, a surprise weapon.

approach.notes: Almost never played by strong players.

level.notes: Dubious so not beginner; a cheap trap line.

character.reason: An early pawn offer leads to open lines and mutual risk.

gambit.reason: White offers the g4 pawn and Black can keep it with ...Bxg4.

soundness.reason: Strong players consider the g4 push unsound and refuted by accurate play.

structure.reason: Pieces fight on open lines after Black takes the pawn.

approach.reason: Hardly ever chosen by strong players.

level.reason: Dubious lines are never Beginner and there is little to learn.

plans.reason: White gives a pawn for development and attack.
